title: A vault's first deposit can be frontrunned to grief deposits below a treshold
Lack of Implementation of Functions in Core Contract Limits Owner Control over NativeVault
body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L46


# Vulnerability details

## **Vulnerability Details:**

The NativeVault contract is deployed by the core contract, which sets itself (core) as the owner of the NativeVault in the [initialize](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L46) function. The owner role allows the core contract to call certain functions on the NativeVault, such as [changeNodeImplementation](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L83), [slashAssets](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L299), [pause](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L322), [unpause](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L328), [pauseNode](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L334), and [unpauseNode](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/NativeVault.sol#L340).

The issue is that the core contract only implements the slashAssets, pause, and unpause functions. Therefore, it is impossible to call the changeNodeImplementation, pauseNode, and unpauseNode functions from the core contract. For instance, the pauseNode function documentation indicates that both the manager and owner should control these functions. However, currently, only the manager, set by the operator, can call this function.

```solidity
    /// @notice Lets the owner or manager of the NativeVault pause NativeNode functions
    /// @param map: 256 bitmap for paused and unpaused functions, 0 to unpause all functions
    function pauseNode(INativeNode node, uint256 map) external onlyRolesOrOwner(Constants.MANAGER_ROLE) {
        node.pause(map);
    }
```

## **Impact:**

The owner will be unable to call essential functions in the NativeVault that they are supposed to manage. This means that if the core contract needs to make changes by calling functions such as changeNodeImplementation, pauseNode, or unpauseNode, it will be unable to do so. This limitation also grants the operator full control over these functions, which is contrary to the intended design and could lead to potential problems.

## **Tools Used:**

- Manual analysis

## **Recommendation:**

Ensure that the core contract implements the missing functions (changeNodeImplementation, pauseNode, unpauseNode). This will allow the owner role to fully control the NativeVault functions as intended.


## Assessed type

Other

body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-karak/blob/f5e52fdcb4c20c4318d532a9f08f7876e9afb321/src/Vault.sol#L78-L119


# Vulnerability details

## Impact 
Share and asset calculations are incorrect, causing initial depositors to lose funds.
The shares per deposited unit of asset will be on an increasing scale so subsequent users get more shares for the same amount of assets; meaning they have a higher claim on the funds in the vault.

## Vulnerability Details
Given that rewards are not added to the vault; shares should always be minted on a 1:1 basis with the assets received.
However, fee-on-transfer tokens charge a fee to users for transfers of the token which breaks this invariant.

This issue affects the two `deposit()` functions and the `mint()` function in Vault.sol.

### Vault::deposit()
The wrong `assets` value is passed to `erc4626::deposit()` to calculate the shares a user will receive.
The actual assets received by the Vault will be less than the input parameter amount so the input param should be adjusted down before sending to `erc4626::deposit()`.

### Vault::mint()
The wrong `assets` amount is returned by `erc4626::mint()`; which calculates the assets a user must pay.
The actual assets received by the Vault will be less than the returned amount so the returned value should be adjusted up in `Vault::deposit()`.

## POC
Vault is set up to accept a Fee-On-Transfer token which has 2% fee

Bob, the first depositor, deposits 1000 tokens
  >> He receives 1000 shares
  >> The vault balance will be 980 tokens

Alice then deposits 1000 tokens 
  >> She receives 1020 Shares
  >> The vault balance will be 1960 tokens

Mike deposits 1000 tokens 
  >> He receives 1030 Shares
  >> The vault balance will be 2940 tokens

## Tools Used
Manual Review
Foundry Testing

## Recommendations
There should be a check in the `deposit()` fucntions whether the token being deposited is fee-on-transfer.
If the token is fee-on-transfer; the `assets` param should be adjusted down by the fee amount before sending to `erc4626::deposit()`.

There should be a check in the `mint()` function whether the token being deposited is fee-on-transfer.
If the token is fee-on-transfer; the `assets` param returned by `erc4626::mint()` should be adjusted up by the fee amount.


## Assessed type

ERC20
